title: Three-dimensional J2 uniaxial path, displacement control, and restart equivalence
purpose: Verify that the local radial return, analytical algorithmic tangent, quadrature state, global Newton path, commit policy, and checkpoint restoration operate as one path-dependent finite-element procedure.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain Mises plasticity with linear isotropic hardening

execution.evidence: An uninterrupted path and a path restarted after load factor 0.5 must recover the same displacement, PEEQ, and complete increment history; a homogeneous displacement-controlled bar must reproduce the analytical uniaxial linear-hardening solution.

observables: The final load factor is one and every accepted increment converges.
At least one quadrature point has positive equivalent plastic strain.
Restarted displacement equals uninterrupted displacement within tolerance.
Restarted committed PEEQ equals uninterrupted committed PEEQ within tolerance.
A nonzero prescribed displacement is applied proportionally at partial and complete step factors.
acceptance: Relative and absolute restart differences satisfy the automated test tolerances.
The analytical tangent independently matches a centered derivative of the local return map.
Committed state changes only after a converged global increment.

quantities.name: mean_axial_stress
quantities.description: Analytical stress at axial strain 0.005 for E=200000, initial yield stress 200, and isotropic hardening modulus 2000.

quantities.name: mean_equivalent_plastic_strain
quantities.description: Analytical accumulated plastic strain from the one-dimensional consistency relation.

limitations: This patch is a regression benchmark, not an external NAFEMS validation.
The checkpoint is portable only for a serial run with the same mesh and dof layout.
Plane stress and finite-strain plasticity are outside this benchmark.
